summary:
**AstroPulse** is an autonomous health-monitoring application designed to help astronauts stay healthy during long space missions to the Moon and Mars. In space, astronauts face several health risks, such as radiation exposure, changes in gravity, and isolation. Since communication with Earth can be delayed by up to 22 minutes, they cannot always depend on doctors for immediate medical help.

AstroPulse helps astronauts monitor their daily health by recording blood glucose, heart rate, blood pressure, and sleep patterns. It also includes optical health checks, ultrasound scanning with digital measuring tools, and cognitive tests to check alertness and concentration.

The application uses an interactive 3D body scanner to display health information and an AI-powered virtual flight doctor called **AERIS** to suggest suitable actions, such as exercise, hydration, and other health precautions. With its simple, visual, and interactive design, AstroPulse helps astronauts manage their health independently and safely during space missions.
details:
Project Details

What it does and how it works:

AstroPulse is a health monitoring application designed to help astronauts take care of their health during long space missions. It works offline on tablets and computers, so astronauts can use it even without an internet connection. The application includes the following features:

1. Interactive Body Scanner: Displays a human body diagram where astronauts can select different body parts, such as the eyes, heart, spine, and legs. It explains possible health problems caused by space conditions, such as vision changes, bone loss, and spinal changes, along with ways to manage them.

2. Daily Health Tracking: Allows astronauts to enter and monitor their daily health details, including blood sugar, heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, oxygen levels, and radiation exposure.

3. Optical Health Monitoring: Uses a webcam or simulated sensor data to estimate heart rate, check pupil size, and observe facial swelling caused by fluid changes in zero gravity.

4. Ultrasound Scanning: Includes simulated ultrasound scans of the eyes, veins, bones, and lungs. Astronauts can use digital measuring tools to check measurements without depending on immediate medical support from Earth.

5. NASA Reaction Time Test (PVT): Includes a simple test that measures how quickly astronauts respond to visual signals. This helps identify tiredness and reduced alertness.

6. AI Medical Assistant (AERIS): An AI-based assistant that checks the health information entered by astronauts and suggests suitable actions. It can recommend basic care, guide them through medical procedures, or prepare a health report to send to doctors on Earth when communication is available.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

AstroPulse helps astronauts monitor their health and identify possible problems early. It provides useful guidance when doctors on Earth are not immediately available. This can help prevent minor health issues from becoming serious and allows astronauts to take better care of themselves during long space missions.

Tools and Technologies Used:

  • HTML5: Used to build the structure of the application.
  • CSS3: Used to design the interface with a modern space-themed appearance.
  • JavaScript (ES6+): Used to develop the main features and make the application interactive.
  • HTML Canvas: Used to display health charts and other visual information.
  • SVG: Used to create the interactive human body diagram.
  • Web Audio API: Used to generate alert sounds, heartbeat sounds, and ultrasound effects.
  • MediaDevices API: Used to access the webcam for health monitoring features.
  • Offline Support: The application is built without external libraries, allowing it to run in a modern browser without an internet connection.

Creativity and Factors Considered:

We focused on making AstroPulse simple, interactive, and easy for astronauts to use during long missions.

  • Different Space Environments: Astronauts can select their location, such as deep-space transit, Lunar Gateway, lunar rover, or Mars base. The application adjusts radiation levels, gravity conditions, and communication delays based on the selected environment.
  • Gamification: To make daily health activities more interesting, the application includes a Resilience Score, daily streaks, eight achievement badges, and exercise challenges. These features encourage astronauts to maintain healthy habits throughout their mission.
  • Personalized Registration: Before using the application, astronauts can create their own profile by entering their name, callsign, blood group, and role, and by choosing an avatar.
